newsitem.title: UK: Minor metals winddown as Christmas draws near.
newsitem.headline: Minor metals winddown as Christmas draws near.

text.p: Apart from flurries of interest in cobalt, cadmium and titanium minor metals held in pre-Christmas doldrums as consumers continued to adopt a stand-offish stance.
"They (consumers) are still living hand to mouth," one London minor metal trader said.
However, along with other market operators, the trader forecast brisk business from consumers in 1997.
"This is likely to lift prices across the board," he said.

Recent volatility in cobalt slowed as the market wound down ahead of Christmas. "If anything the market has a tendency to drift lower, though I believe prices have the potential to snap higher," another trader said.
"The fundamental outlook for cobalt is crisp and clear," one trader said.
Russian material sagged slightly on talk of a further shipment of cobalt into Rotterdam warehouses of between 60 and 80 tonnes.
The situation in Zaire remained a focal point.
The return of President Mobuto to his homeland following treatment for prostate cancer in Switzerland in August and his convalescence in France was noted by traders.
However, sources close to European traders had little to add on Mobuto's return.
"We have heard little in the way of news out of Zaire, though the country remains unstable," one trader said.
"Its wait and see...high grade material remains tight and has the potential to flare if conditions in Zaire deteriorate further," the trader added.
Elsewhere, demand from the aerospace industry swung titanium higher, as well as increased offtake by golf club manufacturers.
Dealers said the market is likely to forge ahead near-term.
"Overall demand is good...start looking higher," one trader commented.
Long term contract negotiations, Japanese demand and a hint of speculative buying bolstered cadmium.
Indian and Chinese buying was also seen in the market.
Indium after a year of downside pressure started to creep higher as Japanese players entered the market, while iridium against the backdrop of consumer offtake also eyed higher levels.
Antimony failed to shine and adopted a lower stance, though this was largely due to a lack of interest.

Germanium was dented by news that a Ukrainian rare metals plant will sell 4.33 tonnes of the material over an unspecified time. "Its not going to help the market but so far the market has not strongly reacted," a trader said.
In September Ukraine sold 6.5 tonnes of stockpiled germanium.
